circleTeaser: Nag Panchami tomorrow. Offer milk to the image, never to live snakes. A short home puja is enough.

dpb.sourceRef: Nag Panchami katha — Shravana Shukla Panchami
dpb.confidenceNote: Worship of the nagas on this Panchami is named in the Purana; wall drawings, anthill visits and the milk-for-live-snakes practice are custom or misconception.

en.title: Nag Panchami
en.heroSubtitle: The day the serpent devtas are honoured — with reverence, not fear.
en.deck: Who the nagas are, what the scripture actually asks on this Panchami, and a simple home puja that harms no living creature.
en.introHtml: On the fifth day of Shravana's bright fortnight, the nagas — the serpent devtas of the Puranas — are honoured. The worship is of the deity, offered before an image. It was never meant to involve a living snake. This guide keeps what the texts ask, names what is custom, and corrects the one practice that should end.

blocks.title: Why this day
blocks.text: He who honours the nagas on the Panchami of Shravana — Ananta, Vasuki, Takshaka and the rest — his household knows no fear of serpents.

blocks.title: Who the nagas are
blocks.text: The Puranas name eight great nagas — Ananta, Vasuki, Padma, Mahapadma, Takshaka, Kulika, Karkotaka and Shankha. Ananta bears the earth; Vasuki circles Shiva's neck and served as the rope at the churning of the ocean. Honouring them on this day is an old acknowledgement that the monsoon earth belongs to more creatures than us.

sankalpa.gloss: For the fearlessness and wellbeing of my family, I perform this Nag Panchami puja. Say it in any language you carry in your heart — no Sanskrit required.

steps.title: Bathe and clean the puja space
steps.description: Morning bath, clean clothes. Wipe the altar or a clean patch of wall near the entrance.

steps.title: Place or draw the nag image
steps.description: A printed image or small idol of the Nag Devta works fully. Many homes draw serpent figures with haldi, geru or cow-dung paste on the wall or a wooden board.
steps.note: The wall drawing is regional custom; any respectful image is complete.

dpb.prathaScope: Pan-India — wall and board drawings strongest in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Bengal and the South

steps.title: Take the sankalp
steps.description: Sit facing east. Take water in your right palm, speak the sankalp, and let the water fall.

steps.title: Offer milk, haldi, akshat and flowers — before the image
steps.description: Place a small bowl of milk, haldi-kumkum, unbroken rice and flowers before the image. The offering is to the deity, through the image — never to a living snake.
steps.note: Milk offered at the image is tradition. Milk fed to live snakes harms them — snakes cannot digest it.

steps.title: Recite the names of the ashta nagas
steps.description: Ananta, Vasuki, Padma, Mahapadma, Takshaka, Kulika, Karkotaka, Shankha — spoken once each with folded hands, or read the Nag Panchami katha.

steps.title: Aarti and prasad
steps.description: Light the diya, close with a short aarti, and share the prasad. If you keep a fast today, it opens after this puja or in the evening, as your family observes.

blocks.title: Your fast today

fasting.name: Full-day fast
fasting.description: Kept until the evening puja in many households. Only if your body allows.

fasting.name: Sajal
fasting.description: Water, milk and fruit through the day; one sattvik meal after the puja.

fasting.name: No fast
fasting.description: The puja alone is a complete observance of Nag Panchami. Fasting is optional on this day.

blocks.text: The Panchami asks for worship; the fast is a devotional addition, not a mandate. Choose what suits your body.

myths.question: Should I pour milk on a live snake, or pay someone who carries one?
myths.answer: No. Snakes cannot digest milk — it sickens and often kills them, and captive display snakes suffer badly. The scriptural offering is made before an image. Honouring the naga means not harming one.

myths.question: If I skip Nag Panchami, will 'sarp dosh' or misfortune strike my family?
myths.answer: No text threatens a household for a missed observance. Dosh-nivaran pujas sold on fear are commerce, not Dharma. Observe the day when you can, with devotion.

myths.question: Is it true you must not dig the earth or cut vegetables today?
myths.answer: Setting aside digging and ploughing is an old custom of care for creatures that live in the soil — a gentle pratha, not a rule whose breach brings harm.

hi.title: नाग पंचमी
hi.heroSubtitle: नाग देवताओं के सम्मान का दिन — श्रद्धा से, भय से नहीं।
hi.deck: नाग कौन हैं, शास्त्र इस पंचमी को वास्तव में क्या कहता है, और एक सरल घरेलू पूजा जो किसी जीव को हानि नहीं पहुँचाती।
hi.introHtml: श्रावण शुक्ल पंचमी को पुराणों के नाग देवताओं का पूजन होता है। यह पूजा प्रतिमा के समक्ष, देवता की है — किसी जीवित सर्प की कभी नहीं। यह मार्गदर्शिका शास्त्र की बात रखती है, प्रथा को प्रथा कहती है, और उस एक प्रथा को सुधारती है जिसे समाप्त होना चाहिए।
